citation: C. L. Wasson, Mr. and Mrs. [unintelligable]'s new french cook (LOC's transcription of the caption), stereograph, copyright 1903 (the date in the handwritten caption). Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division, Stereograph Cards, LC-DIG-stereo-1s44451 (item 2022631776).
repository: Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division. Master TIFF 1s44451u.tif (5881 x 3050), read at tile.loc.gov; crops are kept in kevinrhaas/chicago-evidence evidence/people-references-2026-11-06/working_woman_1904/.
locator: The left-hand frame: the same young woman kneading dough at the kitchen table, facing the camera at about three metres.
rights_note: LOC rights advisory: 'No known restrictions on publication.' Published 1903. Used only as a reference picture people are judged against and as the cut of the 1904 working dress (T-3423); nothing is traced or sampled from it.
access_notes: Viewed 2026-11-06 (T-3423) from the master TIFF. Facing the camera: the pale shirtwaist with its white standing collar and dark tie, sleeves pushed up; the ruffled bib apron, dotted, covering the chest and the skirt front; the dark skirt flounced in rows below the table; low dark shoes with a heel. The same studio kitchen set as the card above. A staged studio photograph, not of Chicago or of any named servant.
note: One of the 1904 working-woman reference set's photographs (data/people_match/reference_sets/working_woman_1904.json).

how far a bib reaches up the chest and across it
